Short title, extent and commencement

THE INTER﷓PROVINCIAL TRADE ORDINANCE, 1964
THE
INTER-PROVINCIAL TRADE ORDINANCE, 1964
ORDINANCE No. IV
OF 1964
[Approved by the National Assembly of Pakistan on the 20th
August, 1964, see Gaz, of P., 1964, Ext., pp. 493d-493f.]
[1st July, 1964]
An Ordinance to make provision for enabling the Central
Government to regulate trade and commerce between the Provinces
1. Short title, extent and
commencement.---(1) This Ordinance may be called the Inter-Provincial Trade
Ordinance, 1964.
(2) It extends to the whole of
Pakistan.
(3) It shall come into force at
once.

Power of Central Government to regulate inter-Provincial Trade

THE INTER﷓PROVINCIAL TRADE ORDINANCE, 1964
THE
INTER-PROVINCIAL TRADE ORDINANCE, 1964
ORDINANCE No. IV
OF 1964
[Approved by the National Assembly of Pakistan on the 20th
August, 1964, see Gaz, of P., 1964, Ext., pp. 493d-493f.]
[1st July, 1964]
An Ordinance to make provision for enabling the Central
Government to regulate trade and commerce between the Provinces
2. Power of Central Government
to regulate inter-Provincial Trade.---(1) Notwithstanding anything
contained in the Essential Commodities Act, 1957, or any other law for the time
being in force, the Central Government, if it so deems necessary or expedient,
may, by general or special order, regulate the movement and transport of any
commodity or class or description of commodities, including imported
commodities, between the Provinces, III of 1957.
(2) Without prejudice to the
generality of the powers conferred by sub-section (1), an order made
thereunder, may provide,-
(a) for
regulating by licences, permits or otherwise the transport and movement of any
commodity or any specified class or description of commodities ;
(b) for
allocating or directing any person or authority to allocate in such manner as
may be specified in the order, space on any ship or aircraft for the carriage
of any commodity or any specified class or description of commodities ;
(c) for
collecting any information or statistics with a view to regulating or
determining any of the afore said matters ; and
(d) for any
incidental or supplementary matters, including, in particular, the entering,
and search of premises, vehicles, vessels and aircraft, the seizure by any
person authorised to make such search of any articles in respect of which such
person has reason to believe that a contravention of the order has been, is
being or is about to be committed, or any records connected therewith, the
grant or issue of licences, permits or other documents.

Delegation of powers

THE INTER﷓PROVINCIAL TRADE ORDINANCE, 1964
THE
INTER-PROVINCIAL TRADE ORDINANCE, 1964
ORDINANCE No. IV

[Approved by the National Assembly of Pakistan on the 20th

An Ordinance to make provision for enabling the Central

3. Delegation of powers.---The
Central Government may, by order in writing, direct that the power to make
borders under section 2 shall, in relation to such matters and subject to such conditions,
if any, as may be specified in the direction, be exercisable also by-
(a) such officer
or authority subordinate to the Central Government, or
(b) such
Provincial Government or such officer or authority subordinate to a Provincial
Government,
as may be specified in the
direction.

Penalties

THE INTER﷓PROVINCIAL TRADE ORDINANCE, 1964
THE
INTER-PROVINCIAL TRADE ORDINANCE, 1964
ORDINANCE No. IV
OF 1964
[Approved by the National Assembly of Pakistan on the 20th
August, 1964, see Gaz, of P., 1964, Ext., pp. 493d-493f.]
[1st July, 1964]
An Ordinance to make provision for enabling the Central
Government to regulate trade and commerce between the Provinces
4. Penalties. If any
person contravenes any order made under section 2, he shall be punishable with
imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years or with fine or with
both, and if the order so provides, any Court trying such contravention may
direct that property in respect of which the Court is satisfied that the order
has been contravened shall be forfeited to the Central Government.
sections.punishment:
punishable with
imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years or with fine or with
both, and if the order so provides, any Court trying such contravention may
direct that property in respect of which the Court is satisfied that the order
has been contravened shall be forfeited to the Central Government.

5. Attempts and abetments.--Any
person who attempts to contravene, or abets a contravention of, any order made
under section 2 shall be deemed to have contravened that order.

Offences by Corporations

THE INTER﷓PROVINCIAL TRADE ORDINANCE, 1964
THE
INTER-PROVINCIAL TRADE ORDINANCE, 1964
ORDINANCE No. IV
OF 1964

Government to regulate trade and commerce between the Provinces
6. Offences by Corporations.
If the person contravening an order made under section 2 is a company or other
body corporate, every director, manager, secretary or other officer or agent thereof
shall, unless he proves that the contravention took place without his knowledge
or that he exercised all due diligence to prevent such contravention, be deemed
to be guilty of such contravention.

Cognizance of offences

7. Cognizance of offences.--No
Court shall take cognizance of any offence punishable under this Ordinance
except upon a complaint in writing made by the Central Government or any person
authorized by the Central Government in this behalf.
sections.punishment:
punishable under this Ordinance
except upon a complaint in writing made by the Central Government or any person
authorized by the Central Government in this behalf.

8. Powers to try offences
summarily.--Any magistrate empowered for the time being to try in a summary
way the offence specified in sub-section (1) of section 260 of the Code of
Criminal Procedure, 1898, may, on application in this behalf being made by the
prosecution, try in accordance with the provisions contained in sections 262 to
265 of the said Code any offence punishable under this Ordinance, V of 1898.
sections.punishment: punishable under this Ordinance, V of 1898.

9. Protection of action taken
under the Ordinance.---(1) No suit, prosecution or other legal proceeding
shall lie against any person for anything which is in good faith done or
intended to be done in pursuance of any order made under section 2.
(2) No suit or other legal
proceeding shall lie against Government for any damage caused or likely to be
caused by anything which is in good faith done or intended to be done in
pursuance of any order made under section 2.

order as is referred to in section 2 made by the Central Government before the

this Ordinance were in force at the time of making such order, but nothing in
